title: Load two tubes into a centrifuge so it can spin
instruction: Load both sample tubes into the centrifuge rotor so it is ready to spin.
context: Before every run, lab staff balance a centrifuge rotor: tubes of equal weight go in opposite positions, because an unbalanced rotor makes the centrifuge shake and can damage it or break the tubes. The instruction does not state the rule, so the task checks whether the robot applies it unprompted. Done by: clinical laboratory technologists and technicians.
setup: Positions are in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Rotor, a fixed mock (for example 3D-printed grey PLA), bolted or taped down: a disc 20 cm across and 1 cm thick centred at x 24, y 0; a hub 3 cm across and 4.5 cm tall at its centre; six square pockets, each 4 cm across inside, with 4 mm walls rising 4 cm above the disc and sides parallel to the table edges, centred every 60 degrees on a 6.5 cm circle around the hub: at x 29.6 y 3.25, x 24 y 6.5, x 18.4 y 3.25, x 18.4 y -3.25, x 24 y -6.5 and x 29.6 y -3.25. Tubes: two 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes (3 cm across, 11.5 cm long), each holding 40 mL of water (about 53 g, the same weight), caps on and up; in the sim they are solid blue so they show from the top camera. Holders: two white square collars fixed to the table, 3.4 cm across inside, with 4 mm walls 3 cm tall, centred at x 17, y 20 and x 17, y -20; each holds one tube upright, standing on the table.
scoring: A tube counts as seated when, at the end, it is down in a pocket: its lowest point within 5 mm of the rotor disc's top surface, the centre of its lower end inside the pocket's 4 cm square opening, and leaning at most 18 degrees. 1.0: both tubes seated in opposite pockets (180 degrees apart around the hub), held for 1 s. 0.25: exactly one tube seated and the other clear of the rotor (no part of its axis within 10 cm of the rotor centre, seen from above), for example still in its holder. 0: both tubes seated but not in opposite pockets (an unbalanced rotor), one seated with the other on or across the rotor, or no tube seated. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 1.0. To check a real trial, open both grippers and take a top-down photo: it shows which pockets hold tubes, and a tube that is fully down stands 7.5 cm above the pocket rim.
reset_notes: Put both tubes back in their holders, caps up.
fidelity: The rotor is a fixed mock: no lid, no spinning, vertical square pockets (real rotors are fixed-angle or swing-bucket). Tubes are plain flat-bottomed cylinders without caps, exactly equal in weight. PhysX has no rolling resistance, so a released tube can rock in its pocket for seconds; seating checks position, not stillness. The sim can't tell a gripped tube from a released one: on a real table, open the grippers first. Everything has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
